Network among exposure-associated features

Source: R/network-build.R
run_exposure_network.Rd

Pre-selects the transcripts and metabolites associated with an exposure, by stability selection or univariate testing, and estimates a cross-omic network among the selected features only. Cheng et al. (2024) analysed transcriptomic and metabolomic signatures of air pollution in two such stages: features associated with the exposures were identified first, and conditional multi-omic networks estimated afterwards.

Usage

run_exposure_network(
  x,
  metabolites,
  celltype,
  exposure,
  celltype_col = "cell_type",
  covariates = NULL,
  selection_method = c("stability", "univariate"),
  fdr_threshold = 0.05,
  pi_threshold = 0.6,
  stability_q = NULL,
  min_cells = 10L,
  network_method = c("coglasso", "block_glasso"),
  lambda_w = 0.3,
  lambda_b = 0.5,
  transform = c("vst", "log_cpm"),
  genes = NULL
)

Arguments

x

SingleCellExposomeExperiment. Each cell's donor is read from the colData column named by sampleColumn(x).

metabolites

Numeric matrix, or a data frame of numeric columns; rows = donors, cols = metabolites. Row names must be donor IDs. A matrix without columns, or a missing or infinite value for an analysed donor, is an error, and so is a column with the name of another column or of a candidate gene: two nodes cannot have the same name. Leave the exposure itself out of the columns: a column that holds the values of the exposure, or a monotone transform of them, has a rank correlation of 1 or -1 with it, is always selected and becomes a node.

celltype

Character; cell type to analyse.

exposure

Character; exposure variable name, a column of exposureData(x); another name is an error.

celltype_col

Character; cell type column. Default "cell_type".

covariates

Character vector or NULL; columns of exposureData(x). The selection is made given the covariates (see Details), and they are regressed out of the transcript and metabolite values before the network is estimated; another name is an error, and so is the exposure itself. Donors with a missing covariate value are left out, with a message. A covariate enters the selection by its ranks and the adjustment of the values as the number it is, so either way it is taken as ordered; give a covariate with more than two unordered categories as one 0/1 column for each category but one.

selection_method

Character; "stability" (default) or "univariate".

fdr_threshold

Numeric; FDR threshold for univariate selection. Default 0.05.

pi_threshold

Numeric in (0.5, 1]; minimum proportion of subsamples in which a feature must be selected under selection_method = "stability". Default 0.6.

stability_q

Integer or NULL; number of features selected in each subsample under selection_method = "stability". The default NULL uses \(\max(1, \lfloor\sqrt{(2\pi_{thr} - 1)p}\rfloor)\), the largest value for which the Meinshausen-Buhlmann bound on the expected number of falsely selected features is at most 1 (when \((2\pi_{thr} - 1)p \ge 1\)). Here \(p\) is the number of candidate features that vary across the donors with a value of the exposure.

min_cells

Integer; minimum cells per pseudobulk.

network_method

Character; "coglasso" (default) or "block_glasso", the estimator for the network on the selected features. "coglasso" needs at least one selected transcript and metabolite; when only one omic layer is selected the block graphical lasso is used instead, with a warning. Otherwise it requires the coglasso package, version 1.1.0 or later (an error when it is not installed), and chooses the penalties from a 10 by 10 grid with the defaults of coglasso::xstars(). The estimator used is recorded in metadata(result)$network_method.

lambda_w

Numeric; graphical-lasso penalty for pairs of features in the same omic layer, on the correlation scale, for the block graphical lasso (network_method = "block_glasso", or the fallback when only one omic layer is selected). Default 0.3.

lambda_b

Numeric; graphical-lasso penalty for pairs of features in different omic layers, on the correlation scale, for the block graphical lasso. Default 0.5.

transform

Character; the transform of the pseudobulk counts, "vst" (default) or "log_cpm", as in run_celltype_network. The call stops when "vst" cannot be computed; it does not switch to the other transform.

genes

Character vector or NULL; row names of x, the genes that are candidates for the selection, taken after the transform as in run_celltype_network. Fewer candidates leave fewer tests to adjust for and a smaller stability_q. A name that is not a row name of x, or that is the name of more than one row, is an error. Default NULL (all genes).

Value

A CelltypeNetworkResult restricted to exposure-associated features. Its metadata record the expression transform, the covariates, the donors of the network (donors) and the number of them with a value of the exposure (n_donors_exposure), on whom the selection was made, the selection settings, for stability selection pfer_bound, in constant_features the candidates that are constant across the donors with a value of the exposure and so could not be selected, and in selection the penalties of the network: lambda_w and lambda_b for the block graphical lasso, or the size of the grid and the selected_lambda_w, selected_lambda_b and selected_c that coglasso selected, with stars_variability.

Details

Stage 1: Feature selection, among the donors with a value of the exposure. Each transcript and metabolite is screened by its Spearman correlation with the exposure. With covariates it is the partial rank correlation: the ranks of the covariates are regressed out of the ranks of the feature and of the exposure, and the residuals are correlated. A feature without variation across these donors, such as a gene without a count in the cell type, is neither tested nor ranked by either method, and \(p\) below counts the features that vary. "univariate" tests the correlation (asymptotic t approximation, with one degree of freedom fewer for each covariate that is not constant or a combination of the others among these donors) with BH correction over these features. The approximation is poor when both the exposure and a feature take one value in all but a few donors, as an exposure that only a few donors have, or that is above its limit of detection in a few, and a gene with a count in one or two donors: the p-value of such a gene is far too small whenever its donors are among those few, and with many such genes among the candidates some pass the BH correction together. For an exposure of this kind, name the candidate genes with genes and leave out those with a count in few donors. "stability" applies stability selection (Meinshausen and Buhlmann 2010) to a marginal screen: in each of 100 random subsamples of half the donors with an observed exposure, the stability_q features with the largest absolute correlation with the exposure are selected, and features selected in a proportion of at least pi_threshold of subsamples are retained. The screen remains defined when features outnumber donors. Under the exchangeability and better-than-random-guessing assumptions of Meinshausen and Buhlmann, the expected number of falsely selected features is at most \(q^2 / ((2\pi_{thr} - 1)p)\), reported as pfer_bound. Candidates with a count in very few donors are hardly ever among the stability_q highest of a subsample, which the exchangeability assumption does not allow for; with many of them among the candidates the bound is too small. genes can leave them out. At least three features must be selected.

Transcript values are log-CPM or VST values and therefore relative to each donor's library size. When the exposure strongly changes genes that carry a large share of the counts, the remaining genes shift in the opposite direction and can pass the screen; with few measured genes this can dominate the univariate screen.

Stage 2: Network estimation on the selected features only, with collaborative graphical lasso model selection by XStARS ("coglasso") or the block graphical lasso ("block_glasso"). It is one network for all the donors analysed. The exposure is not regressed out of the features and is not a node, so an edge can reflect the association that two features share with the exposure, and the network does not estimate how the dependence between features changes with the exposure.

References

Cheng SL et al. (2024). Multiomic signatures of traffic-related air pollution in London reveal potential short-term perturbations in gut microbiome-related pathways. Environ Sci Technol 58:8771-8782. doi:10.1021/acs.est.3c09148

Meinshausen N, Buhlmann P (2010). Stability selection. J R Stat Soc Series B, 72(4):417-473.

Examples

set.seed(3)
donors <- sprintf("D%02d", 1:20)
donor <- rep(donors, each = 40)
exposure <- stats::setNames(stats::rnorm(20), donors)
counts <- matrix(stats::rpois(20 * length(donor), 20), nrow = 20,
    dimnames = list(paste0("G", 1:20), paste0("c", seq_along(donor))))
## two genes rise and two fall with the exposure
effect <- c(0.8, 0.8, -0.8, -0.8)
for (g in 1:4)
    counts[g, ] <- stats::rpois(length(donor),
        20 * exp(effect[g] * exposure[donor]))
sce <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(donor_id = donor, cell_type = "Mono"))
scee <- build_scee(sce, matrix(exposure, ncol = 1,
    dimnames = list(donors, "PM2.5")), sample_col = "donor_id")
metabolites <- matrix(stats::rnorm(20 * 3), nrow = 20,
    dimnames = list(donors, paste0("M", 1:3)))
metabolites[, "M1"] <- metabolites[, "M1"] + 1.5 * exposure
if (requireNamespace("glasso", quietly = TRUE)) {
    net <- run_exposure_network(scee, metabolites, celltype = "Mono",
        exposure = "PM2.5",
        selection_method = "univariate",
        network_method = "block_glasso",
        transform = "log_cpm")
    net
}
#> [exposomeSC] Exposure network: 5/23 features selected
#> CelltypeNetworkResult for 'Mono'
#>   Method: exposure_restricted
#>   Nodes: 5 (4 transcripts, 1 metabolites)
#>   Edges: 10 (4 cross-omic)
#>   Donors: 20
